Transcription

No runtime

For turning speech into text.

There is no transcription runtime on your devices (Nova looks for whisper.cpp or faster-whisper), so transcription stays off. Nothing is sent elsewhere to transcribe instead.

Decision model

A decision model answers yes-or-no questions about outside content (is this page trying to give Nova instructions?) with a probability. Nova uses its answer only once that exact model has passed Nova’s test for that question; until then, what Nova can’t vouch for is held back as unsure.

Tev1 on this device: Nova couldn’t reach 127.0.0.1:11434: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:11434.

Jev: Jev isn’t set up: no route has been chosen in Settings › Models.

Until a decision model passes a check’s eval, your sorting model answers it, as before.

No decision model has a scorecard here yet: none is in use, so none has been tested on this device’s checks.

Nova recommends Jev jev-1.14.0 through TypeSafe’s own API (https://api.typesafe.ai), and tev1:4b on this device: Tev1 4B, the default: this device has 8.8 GB for models (no GPU Nova can use, so models run on the CPU from 18 GB of memory).

Jev route
Jev model
Jev key

The key is kept in Nova’s vault and never shown again. No call is made to Jev until a route and a key are set.

Tev1 size
Let Nova choose for this device
Tev1 4B
Tev1 0.8B
Screening: let Jev judge outside content in local modes

While this is on, outside content Nova screens (pages, mail, files, tool output) is sent to TypeSafe’s cloud (Jev) to be judged, even in local-first and local-only. Local-only isn’t strictly local for screening while it is on.

Screening covers pages, mail, files and tool output. Text from Capture (screen text and meeting transcripts) never goes to Jev, in any mode: only your local models and Nova’s own checks screen it.

Box (preview): let Jev judge images

While this is on, images Nova is asked to judge, including camera and screen frames from sources you have allowed, are sent to TypeSafe’s cloud (Jev) in cloud and local-first modes. In local-only they never go to a cloud provider. TypeSafe labels images and Box a preview.

Sources, consent, and what Nova remembers

CAPTURE

What Nova may see on your devices, for context. Each source starts turned off, and the top bar shows when capture is on. What is captured is kept on your own devices.

Off.

Open Capture
Sources

No source yet. A paired computer lists what it can capture here once its device agent says so.

Screenpipe’s address
API key (if Screenpipe asks for one)

If Screenpipe runs on this computer, Nova can take in what it records. It stays off until you turn it on.

Add Screenpipe
What each kind of device can capture
Never captured

Private and incognito windows, always: Nova recognises them by the window’s title, in the major browsers’ common languages. That is a best effort, so also list them in Screenpipe’s own ignored-windows setting, which stops Screenpipe recording them at all. Password managers and banking apps and sites, recognised by their names and addresses: also a best effort. And anything you list here.

Before it is kept, text shaped like a key, a token, a password, a card or bank account number is blanked out, in the words, the window title and the address. Then a model on this computer or your own network checks the rest for passwords, keys and someone’s money or health details. Until a model trusted for that has checked it, captured text is held: kept on your devices like the rest of capture, not added to memory.

Security

Passkeys that confirm tier-3 actions here

SECURITY
PASSKEYS FOR TIER-3 ACTIONS

Tier-3 actions on Nova’s own screen ask for a passkey, and nothing tier-3 runs until you add one. Your browser will ask you to create it with your security key, fingerprint or screen lock. Nova keeps only its public key. Add two, so losing one never locks you out.

Backups and changes

Backup folders, checkpoints, restores and changes

Backups
BACKUP COPIES

No backup folders selected. Choose a backup folder to keep copies outside Nova.

Backup folder

A private folder that already exists, outside Nova’s home and not containing it.

Copies to keep

Keep 1–365 copies. Older copies are removed as new ones arrive.

Encrypted copy folder

A different folder that already exists. Choose a backup folder first.

Save backup settings

Remove a folder explicitly to stop using it. An empty or invalid entry does not remove a saved folder. Saved files stay on disk.

RECOVERY KEY

For encrypted backup copies. It does not replace Nova Vault recovery factors.

Recovery key

Set up an encrypted copy folder to get its recovery key.

BACKUPS

Checkpoints

A checkpoint is everything Nova keeps on this computer: memories, tasks, settings, its keys. It stays on this computer. Nova takes one by itself before it changes itself, upgrades or restores, and you can take your own.

Nova keeps the newest 10 automatic checkpoints, counted in the order they were taken, never by date, and every checkpoint you name until you delete it. A new checkpoint is complete before an old one is removed, and a named one is never removed to make room.

Name
Take a checkpoint

No checkpoints yet.

CHANGES

A change to Nova goes through these steps: tried on a copy first, tested, released as a version, and watched live before it stays. If a check fails, Nova puts back what was there before.

No changes yet. When Nova or you propose one, it shows here with every check it went through.

Checkpoints

A checkpoint is everything Nova keeps on this computer: memories, tasks, settings, its keys. It stays on this computer. Nova takes one by itself before it changes itself, upgrades or restores, and you can take your own.

Nova keeps the newest 10 automatic checkpoints, counted in the order they were taken, never by date, and every checkpoint you name until you delete it. A new checkpoint is complete before an old one is removed, and a named one is never removed to make room.
